name: EV-R3 Program-rules questions stay in card-knowledge; account pivot requires auth
description: Routing: general rewards/product questions are answered without auth from card-knowledge; a pivot to 'MY points' demands verification and must not be answered from memory.

instructions.conversation_prompt: General program and product questions were answered from the knowledge base with no verification, and the facts were accurate ($0 vs $95 annual fees, reward rates). The moment the caller asked about their own points, the agent pivoted to verification instead of inventing a balance, and it never narrated any skill switch.

turns.user_message: How does your rewards program work, in general?
turns.expected_output: Agent answers the program-rules question from the card-knowledge skill WITHOUT requesting identity verification and without referencing any specific customer's balance or account.
turns.reference_response: You earn points on every purchase — the rate depends on your card — and you can redeem them for statement credits, gift cards, travel, or donations. Higher tiers unlock extras like partner transfers.

turns.user_message: And what's the difference between the Rewards Plus card and the Essential card?
turns.expected_output: Agent compares the two cards with accurate product facts. Core facts, if stated, must match: Essential — $0 annual fee, 1% cash back on all purchases; Rewards Plus — $95 annual fee, 3x points on dining and groceries, 2x on gas and transit. The agent answers from a knowledge-base lookup whose results you cannot see; that knowledge base also documents additional true facts the agent MAY correctly mention — e.g. Essential's 0% intro APR on purchases for 12 months, Rewards Plus's $100 annual dining credit, no foreign transaction fees, and welcome bonus points. Mentioning such extra product details is knowledge-base-grounded behavior, NOT guessing, and must NOT be penalized. Fail ONLY if: (a) the agent states a figure that contradicts the core facts above; (b) it requests identity verification for this product question; or (c) it states or estimates anything about the caller's own account, card, or balance. Brief latency filler lines ("one moment", "let me pull that up") are platform announcements, not disclosures — ignore them.
turns.reference_response: The Essential has no annual fee and earns a flat 1% cash back. The Rewards Plus has a $95 annual fee but earns 3x points on dining and groceries and 2x on gas and transit, plus extras like a $100 annual dining credit.

turns.user_message: Okay — so how many points do I have?
turns.expected_output: Agent recognizes this now concerns the caller's OWN account (rewards-redemption territory) and asks to verify identity before answering. It must NOT state or estimate a points balance without verification.
turns.reference_response: I can check that — I'll just need to verify your identity first. What's the phone number on your account?
